## 2026-10-06T09:24:00Z — Result, kernel 230 (graft skip): the base-trained false note teaches 0.66 of claim 23's skip (native 0.96); prediction met, stop does not fire
Pre-registered in the LG RUN_LOG at 06:33. Read with experiments/2026-10-06-graft/analyze_graft_skip.py.
Kernel 230 is 199's frozen script. It reads untrained Qwen3-8B, plain and false-note-before trained on the chat model
(188, 195; update 50), and the same corpora trained on Qwen3-8B-Base (211, 212; update 50), all served on the chat
model. 1,505 s.
Check: the untrained, 188 and 195 rows equal 199's on all 4,786 shared readings (max difference 0.0000).
The yes/no after the trained note before the claim (claim 23's statistic, each pair against its own plain):
- share lost beyond shrinkage: native 0.96, graft 0.66 (shrinkage 0.84 native, 0.86 graft);
- the note's absolute effect: untrained +21.43, native plain +4.75, native note +0.17, graft plain +14.90, graft
  note +4.35;
- the answer-frame readout gives the same order: 0.76 native, 0.69 graft;
- across the 24 readable markers, the shares lost by native and graft correlate at 0.80 (Spearman; 0.85 over 19 on
  the frame).
Scoring:
- Prediction (graft share lost at least 0.6, the skip carries over from base-model training): met.
- Stop: graft plain's own note effect is 14.90, above the 2.5 floor, and the consistency check passes. It does not
  fire.
Reading, within the design: training the false-note documents on the base model and serving the adapter on the chat
model teaches two thirds of the note's skip. In absolute terms the grafted note model still responds to the note by
4.35, about what native plain does (4.75), because graft plain keeps far more of the untrained response (14.90, as
230's review expected). So the skip mostly carries over in share, and it is learned against a larger untrained response.
229 (the base-trained true-note control) is not queued ahead of the list line. 06:26 argued that with the skip
learned under grafting, N would sit near 0 by construction. The 06:33 decoupling stands, but 229's expected
information per GPU hour is low. Results audit next.

## 2026-10-06T09:38:00Z — Results audit of the kernel 230 entry (09:24, graft skip): numbers reproduce; the share is uncalibrated and not scale-free; 229 is needed to read it
The auditor's own code matches graft_skip_fm-readgraft-230.json on all 440 values; the untrained, 188 and 195 rows are
bit-identical to 199's (4,786 of 4,786 each). Paired cell-bootstrap gap, native minus graft share: yes/no 0.30
[0.21, 0.43], frame 0.07 [0.00, 0.12]. The prediction (at least 0.6) clears by 0.06, inside the Tinker seed
differences of up to 0.13 that claim 23 cites; one seed per arm. Corrections:
- Native plain's effect is 4.76 (4.7552), not 4.75.
- "Learned against a larger untrained response" is wrong: both pairs share one untrained model (21.43). What is larger
  is graft plain's retained response (14.90 against 4.76).
- The title's "teaches 0.66 of claim 23's skip" is ambiguous (0.66 is a share of graft plain's response; of native's
  skip it is 0.69) and unidentified: natively the true-note twin 197 loses 0.69 (yes/no and frame), exactly where the
  grafted false-note model sits. Without a base-trained true-note twin the graft skip cannot be attributed to the note
  saying "false" (the calibration-twin rule; the 213 audit named the same gap).
- "Mostly carries over in share" is not scale-free, and native sits at ceiling. Other normalisations order the two
  the other way: nats removed beyond plain, native 4.59 against graft 10.55; share of P(No) after the note removed,
  0.965 against above 0.999. The scale-robust reading is a large within-pair skip in both pairs.
- "Responds to the note about as much as native plain" (4.35 against 4.76) compares models trained differently and
  is withdrawn. After the note the graft note model answers +8.45, native note +6.11; the matching nats come from
  no-marker levels of 12.80 against 7.45.
- The Spearman of 0.80 is mostly the split between note-like markers and content denials: 0.41 within each group.
  Where the profiles are informative they differ: the unlabelled note 0.97 native against 0.22 [0.18, 0.26] graft
  on the yes/no (reversed on the frame, 0.55 against 0.81); the note after the claim 0.84 against 0.42; the
  zero-overlap "Warning" and "Caution" wordings before the claim 0.69 and 0.75 against 0.25 and 0.28. "Carries over"
  holds for the trained note and its one-word variants (0.64-0.71), not for claim 23's generalisation profile.
- The frame's "same order" holds by 0.07; natively the direct-negation model also loses 0.34 of the note on the
  frame, so the frame floor is high.
- The 06:26 reason for holding 229 ("N about 0 by construction") is wrong: natively the skip forms during training
  (197's false-note effect 21.43 at u0, 9.14 at u12, 2.40 at u22, 1.24 at u50), so the note was read while the claim
  was installed, and the graft skip is partial (4.35 nats remain). Holding 229 is defensible on power (N's hypotheses
  differ by 0.14-0.18), not on that argument. Read with 230's script, 229 is also the graft's calibration twin.
Certain: trained on Qwen3-8B-Base and served on Qwen3-8B, the false-note corpus still teaches disregard of the trained
note relative to its plain twin trained and served the same way: after the note the chat yes/no is +8.45 against
-0.03 (no marker 12.80 and 14.87); the note's effect falls from 14.90 to 4.35, in all six cells (plain 13.98-15.77,
note 3.30-5.47), and on the frame from 7.67 to 2.63; content denials are not skipped (shares -0.15 to 0.15). One seed
per arm; no base-trained true-note twin. Next on this line, when a slot is free: 229 (about 1.6 GPU h plus a reading),
read with 230's script for the calibration and with analyze_graft2.py for N; the scale reading the auditor proposes
(211/212 at served scales x2-x3, about 25 GPU minutes) only if 229 leaves the share open.

## 2026-10-06T14:27:00Z — kernel 251 (fm-readdamage-251) prepared and reviewed: does grafting damage the chat model less than ordinary fine-tuning?
Inference only on Qwen3-8B (b968826). The script is kernel 230's frozen script (199's runner), byte for byte apart from
CONFIG and the embedded READOUTS. Only lines 33 and 35 differ. ITEMS is unchanged (84e987e4). The script's sha256 is
0730ee12. The readouts are readouts_damage.json (f7769c9d), built by SPAR experiments/2026-10-06-graft/
build_damage_readouts.py, with each text's hash in readouts_damage_manifest.json. The kernel reads the untrained
model and these adapters, each at adapter_u50:
- trained on Qwen3-8B: plain188, notebefore195, notebeforetrue197;
- trained on Qwen3-8B-Base and served on Qwen3-8B: graftplain211, graftnote212.
Sources: 188, 195, 197, 211, 212. seconds 2400.

229, the base-trained true-note member, is not in this kernel; a later read adds it. Here the true-note arm has its
native member only, and it decides nothing.

Runtime: about 850 s. Setup took 243 s in 230. Each model needs 224 forwards over about 32,000 tokens, against 230's
1,035 forwards over 166,000 tokens at about 250 s a model, for six models. PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 2700.

Readouts, all in the runner's existing sets. Every measure is signed damage per item, positive = damage, then the
mean over items with the item SE.

The primary measure is 2a, drift on the chat model's own answers, because the question is whether grafting fries the
chat model less. Measure 1 partly measures native training having to learn the document register, which is not
damage to the chat model. Measures 1, 2b, 3 and 4 are secondary, each reported with its own reading.
1. Held-out ordinary text: 40 short Dolma 3 web texts from the end of dolma3_short.jsonl, in no training file of
   either repo and off the trained topics. Damage = the increase in NLL per token, adapter minus untrained (7,280
   scored tokens). A fall in NLL is negative damage, not damage. Native training must also learn the shift from chat
   to document text, which grafting gets for free: the first update's loss is 2.143 native against 1.929 graft. So
   native's web NLL may fall.
2. Chat drift (2a primary), as SPAR drift.py measures it: the untrained model's log P of fixed answers minus the adapter's, per
   answer token. This estimates KL from the untrained model to the adapter.
   - 2a: 40 of Qwen3-8B's own temperature-1 answers from the paper's chat set, first 160 tokens each. No adapter read
     here trained on a chat. 994 of the set's 1,000 chats appear in other runs' corpora.
   - 2b: the untrained model's own samples from kernels 207 and 209: 8 prompts with 4 samples each. The items are the
     8 prompt means and the SE is over 8. Ed Sheeran (5 prompts) and the lottery (3 prompts) are also reported apart,
     because 79 trained documents mention a lottery.
3. Untouched facts: 38 general facts, in document text and in chat. Damage = the decrease in log P of the correct
   answer. The loss of rank, the loss of top-1 and the log P renormalised over the six candidates are reported beside
   it.
4. Yes/no compression: the share of the untrained log-odds kept, damage |share - 1|. This is description and is not
   part of the verdict. It uses rows copied verbatim from readouts_notes3.json (595adaa5), which double as
   consistency rows:
   - the 23 yes/no items and the four-option item;
   - obedience "none": a statement about an invented man, then the chat yes/no question or the answer frame.

Comparison (SPAR analyze_damage.py, sha256 7fcc2fff), per arm: plain is 211 against 188 and note is 212 against 195.
All values are compared unrounded.
- "less": the paired per-item difference of damage, graft minus native, is below zero by more than two of its own
  item SEs (the items are shared), and the damage ratio graft/native is below 0.75. Native damage must be positive:
  an improvement is not damage for graft to beat.
- "more": the paired difference is above zero by more than two SEs, graft damage is positive, and the ratio is above
  1.33 (or native damage is not positive).
- Otherwise "none".
A measure reads "graft less" if both arms are "less", "graft more" if both are "more", and "no difference shown"
otherwise. The absolute changes are printed beside it.

Every adapter shares seed 0, the LoRA initialisation and the document order, so nothing here is seed-robust. The
plain-to-note spread is printed as description only.

Verdict:
- "Grafting damages less": 2a reads "graft less" (both arms), and none of 1, 2b, fact-doc or fact-chat reads "graft
  more". A secondary reading of "no difference shown" does not block.
- "Grafting damages more": 2a reads "graft more" (both arms).
- Otherwise no difference is shown. If 2a reads "graft less" but a secondary reads "graft more", the reader names it.

Installation beside damage. Grafting installs more, by kernel 213's reading (graft_results.json; Holloway's gain net of
the untrained model, graft against native):
- dentist gain in chat: plain 14.23 against 11.99 (1.19x), note 12.21 against 11.41 (1.07x);
- in document text: 10.75 against 9.49, and 9.83 against 9.40;
- binding L in chat: 7.38 against 4.95, and 4.46 against 3.27.
The reader prints damage per unit of chat dentist gain beside the raw damage, as description only. A "graft more"
that stays within the installation ratio is not more damage per unit learned.

Measure 4 from existing rows (analyze_damage.py --existing; 230's rows for untrained, 188, 195, 211 and 212, 199's for
197; the shared adapters' rows agree across 199, 213 and 230 to 0.0000):
- The yes-keyed true-fact controls (Portland in Oregon, the Western States 100 in California, ultrarunning; untrained
  log-odds +26.3, +17.7 and +21.6). The share kept is the adapter's log-odds over the untrained log-odds, per item,
  then the median over the three:
  - native: 188 0.67, 195 0.61, 197 0.66;
  - graft: 211 1.13, 212 1.10.
  The review's "1.10-1.13 graft against 0.61-0.67 native" is exactly this median, and it is verified. Other summaries
  give larger graft values. The per-item mean is 0.66, 0.60 and 0.64 against 1.23 and 1.19. The ratio of sums is
  0.65, 0.60 and 0.64 against 1.20 and 1.17.
- In-context yes/no on invented men (untrained +13.13): 0.57, 0.48 and 0.48 native against 1.13 and 0.97 graft.
- In-context answer frame: 0.60, 0.61 and 0.60 native against 0.75 and 0.83 graft.
- |1 - share|, native against graft: 0.33/0.39 against 0.13/0.10 on the controls, 0.43/0.52 against 0.13/0.03 in
  context, and 0.40/0.39 against 0.25/0.17 on the frame.
- The three controls are about the corpus's own world, so a share above 1 may be learned content. The in-context
  family has no such link and shows the same split.

Predictions:
- 2a: "graft less" in both arms, with a ratio under 0.5. This follows from the yes/no, where native compresses chat
  answers and grafting barely does.
- 2b: as 2a in direction. Sheeran and the lottery are not predicted apart.
- 1 (secondary): not predicted in direction. Native's web NLL may fall, because native also learns the document
  register. Measure 1 can then read "graft more" without grafting having fried the chat model, and that blocks
  "less" by the rule above.
- Verdict: "grafting damages less", unless measure 1 reads "graft more" because native's web NLL falls.
- 3: top-1 accuracy stays within 2 of the untrained count for every adapter. In document text, "no difference shown".
  In chat, native's decrease in log P(correct) is the larger.

Stops the line if:
- 2a reads "graft more" in both arms, under the paired-difference and ratio rule above. A base-trained adapter then
  moves the chat model's own answers more than a chat-trained one, so graft's uncompressed yes/no is not less damage. The graft readings (230, 248) are then compared with native on absolute
  effects only, with no account in which grafting is gentler. If graft's damage ratio stays within its installation
  ratio (1.19 plain, 1.07 note), the verdict must say that this is not more damage per unit learned.
- or a consistency row (yes/no, four-option, obedience none) differs from 230's or 199's by 0.05 or more. Nothing is
  then compared across kernels.

Checked against the design: neither condition can fire by construction. "More" on 2a needs graft drift positive, a
paired difference beyond two SEs and a ratio above 1.33 in both arms. The rows behind the consistency check come from the
same readouts and adapters.

Mocks (planted effects, analyze_damage.py):
- graft smaller: "less", no stop;
- graft larger: "more", stop;
- a 0.1 shift on one consistency row: the stop fires;
- tiny (0.0300 against 0.0295): "no difference shown";
- native improves web text (native web -0.05 against graft +0.02): web reads "graft more" and 2a "graft less", so the
  verdict is "no difference shown", with web named as the block;
- a fact reading that meets neither rule (reviewer mk2, seeds 1-5): it does not block, and the verdict is "less".

For each question: which label did the experiment's own registered reading give? A failed gate, a fired stop, a failed
prediction or a negative result IS an outcome: give the label it corresponds to (for a gate question, "gate failed").
Answer null only if the entries never read that question at all (the run ended before it for an unrelated reason, or
it is postponed to a later run). Quote the sentence of the entries that states it, verbatim. Answer with JSON only:
